name: Salt & Straw
notes: Little Italy location. Prices extracted from Uber Eats catalog JSON embedded in the page (priceTagline fields), not full JSON.parse (a nested metaJson field breaks strict parsing) - used targeted regex extraction instead. Menu has two overlapping pint tiers with different prices for what appear to be the same or similar flavors: 'Classic Pints' at $14.75 (11 core flavors) and a second 'Ice Cream Pints' section listing additional pie-collaboration flavors plus 3 items - Salted Malted Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough, Sea Salt with Caramel Ribbons, Coffee and Love Nuts - priced at $11.80 with slightly different item-name text/capitalization than their $14.75 Classic Pints counterparts. Per standing rule, these were kept as distinct line items rather than merged since exact captured text and price differ; exact duplicate name+price captures (from the same items appearing twice in the underlying page data) were excluded rather than double-counted. Prices are Uber Eats delivery marketplace prices, not verified in-store prices.

name: Rockin' Baja Lobster - Gaslamp
notes: PDF menu is a scrambled multi-column layout (plain pdftotext, no -layout, misattributes some columns' trailing prices to the wrong item). Cross-verified every filed name/price pair against the pdftotext -layout column positions to confirm correct pairing before filing. Filed only the 3 sections where every item's price could be confirmed via matching column position: Starters & Buckets (12 items), Baja Buns & Bowls (6 items), Soup/Salad/Sides (8 items) = 26 items. Deliberately excluded the Signature Baja Buckets, Palapa Platters, Tacos/Burritos, and Beverages/Cocktails sections - their columns interleave unpredictably (confirmed one clear cross-column misattribution: a bucket's $89-for-2 price nearly got attached to 'Mexican Crab Raggoons') and prices could not be paired with confidence. Some items have optional add-on upcharges (e.g. Rockin' Works Burger $21, +$2 for sliced avocado; Caesar Salad $13, +$6 to add chicken) - only the base price was filed, add-ons omitted.

name: The Cheesecake Factory
notes: DoorDash JSON-LD for this store is severely truncated (only 91 of ~423 catalog items serialize into the standard ld+json Menu block, missing ~23 of 31 real menu categories per the embedded menuCategories metadata). Full item list recovered via regex extraction of the raw HTML's inline escaped JSON catalog blob (name/description/displayPrice fields plus each item's logging.fieldsMap container_name), matched against menuCategories section counts. Section-header false positives (item name equal to its own container_name) were filtered out. A residual ~26-item bucket lacking a nearby container_name was cross-checked against all sectioned items: ~22 were exact name+price duplicates of items already filed under their real section (dropped as redundant) or non-item JSON-parsing artifacts (dropped: a corrupted "$14.50 All Day..." fragment that was actually a slice of the menuList/menuCategories metadata block, and a garbage "The Cheesecake Factory $19.95" self-referential match). The remaining 4 (Fettuccini Alfredo with Chicken $33.95, Chicken Madeira $30.95, Cajun Salmon* $34.95, Steak Diane $33.95) were confirmed real items appearing a second time elsewhere in the page with an intact logging block, from which their true section was recovered directly (Pastas, Specialties, Fish & Seafood, Steaks respectively) rather than inferred by name. Confidence set to medium (marketplace source, not first-party) despite the unusually large recovery effort; no prices were invented, merged, or divided — every price is a displayPrice value read directly from the page.

name: Rodizio Grill Brazilian Steakhouse San Diego
notes: Rodizio-style Brazilian steakhouse: unlimited rotisserie meats and gourmet salad bar served per-person, not itemized by dish. This location's own official page publishes fixed per-person tier pricing (Full Rodizio, Salad-bar-only, Children), split by lunch/dinner daypart, which is treated as the priced menu. The national rodiziogrill.com/menu.aspx page explicitly defers to per-location pages for pricing ("For pricing, click here and choose your favorite location"), confirming the location page is the authoritative first-party price source. Children 0-2 yrs are free with a paying adult (no price to record).

name: Yogurt Mill
blocked: The restaurant's own priced menu page (yogurt-mill.com/yogurt-menu/) returns HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt (plain browser headers, full browser header set with referer, and Googlebot user-agent all blocked identically) - a bot wall, not a missing/removed page. Confirmed the menu is not a no-price venue: the shop's own blog states verbatim "we don't weigh your yogurt and charge you $15 dollars for one yogurt, we have set affordable prices for you" (fixed pricing, not pay-by-weight), and a Google search snippet of the live menu page shows real priced line items (e.g. "$13.25", "$12.75", "$7.75" against item names including "Banana [Split]" and "Yogurt Shake"), but the snippet is truncated and reorders content, so item/price pairing cannot be trusted without invented interpretation - per the never-merge/never-invent rule these were not recorded as dishes. No DoorDash/Uber Eats/Grubhub listing for this specific El Cajon location (935 Broadway) was found; the Yelp business page also returns 403. Re-attempt when the bot wall can be bypassed or a marketplace listing appears.
